The physiology, biomechanics and rules layer (A06-S1, A06-S2, A06-S3) is the only peer-reviewed, named-sample, dated evidence in 58 signals and it survived attack essentially intact - Sports Medicine 2017 for lateral movement and jump counts, MDPI Sports 2022 (n=140) corroborating the 31% lateral-shuffle figure independently, Baker et al. 2019 (n=1303) for sweat normative data, Baker 2017 for trapped sweat in basketball uniforms specifically, and primary FIBA and NFHS rule text. It is also the layer with the fewest opportunities built on it.

League and event operational data verified against primary releases, with corrections that mostly strengthened the signals: NBL attendance (the league's own 1,231,796 exceeding the Wikipedia figure cited), BAL (140,000+ and 2,739,498 YouTube views, +69%), Unrivaled (ticket revenue +204%, tickets +249%, and a Philadelphia night generating ~USD 1M in tickets plus USD 400,000 in merchandise), Basketball Australia and AusPlay participation.

Product-existence claims are generally accurate where they are positive. Where a specialist said a product or a brand exists, it usually does - ballaholic, Ugat, Know The Culture, Asiya, Li-Ning Wade UPF, adidas Crazy Lite, Nike DNA UV Woven, Sabrina and its plus-size SKU. The failures are almost entirely in the negative direction, in claims that something does NOT exist.

The skeptic layer is itself a first-class asset. It caught source-laundering (Accio, Sportsverse, report mills), metric substitution (49% footwear mindshare reported as apparel mindshare, a 23-point error), order-of-magnitude transcription errors (+60% vs the published +601%), base effects (+34% attendance that is +13% per game), stale dating (2014 quotes, 2019 collections, 2023 tournaments presented as current), and category errors (a Philippine FOOTBALL kit cited as basketball pricing evidence, running shorts cited as basketball best-sellers). Seven independent 'biggest miss' findings converge on one systemic fault, which is itself a reliable meta-finding.

Honest disclosure of environmental limits. The A03 skeptic verified that every consumer and retail web host was blocked for both the specialist and the reviewer, and said so explicitly rather than papering over it. Several specialists correctly flagged their own gaps (no shorts-specific market sizing exists; no quantitative women's fit data was found; no phone-carry behaviour was measured). That candour is what makes this audit possible.
weaknesses: There is no first-party Nike commercial data anywhere in the base. No sell-through, no unit mix by inseam, no markdown rate by SKU, no return rates or return reasons, no realised ASP, no size-curve fill, no repeat-purchase interval, no channel split for the shorts class. Every price position and every length recommendation in every opportunity across seven domains is therefore unanchored - and the same three or four internal pulls would resolve most of the portfolio's open questions at once.

Not one price, spec or review claim in the entire base was confirmed against a retrieved product page. All retail hosts were blocked for every agent, so the price architecture is built from search-result summaries, and at least one figure (the USD 75 Aero-FIT basketball short) appears to be the search engine echoing the query language back. Three mutually incompatible Nike price ladders coexist in the base and none of them came from a page.

Report mills and AI content farms are load-bearing in six of seven domains: the Technavio franchise (verified as one report in four vintages), Verified Market Research, Dataintelo, SkyQuest, market.us, WiseGuy, Market Research Intellect, plus Accio (Alibaba's AI B2B sourcing engine, reused across five signals in two domains), anarchylabel, northyard, compressionathlete (an annually re-dated SEO guide), and ericemanuelsshop (an unofficial site the brand is litigating against). Category sizing estimates from these sources disagree by roughly 2x for the same year and category.

Marketplace listings are repeatedly treated as market data: Amazon best-seller impressions with no rank or unit figures, Foot Locker auto-generated inseam facets read as a merchandising strategy, TikTok Shop listings as cultural evidence, Lazada volume impressions, StockX catalogue pages as proof of a resale market, and a retailer navigation menu as a styling signal.

Consumer voice is thin, biased and tiny where it exists. Review samples of n=3 (Walmart Icon) carry franchise-level quality conclusions; Trustpilot, a complaint-selected venue, is read as sentiment; a single reviewer quote supports a women's fit finding; and the one genuinely usable consumer datapoint in the base (Dick's Icon+ 6" at 3.9 stars with 67% recommending across 64 reviews) was found by a skeptic, not a specialist.

Systematic absence-of-evidence-as-evidence. 'No Nike UPF short exists', 'no Aero-FIT basketball short exists', 'women's length choice exists only via tall sizing', 'pockets are not part of Nike's story', 'Nike has no heritage-length short', 'tournament merch is largely tees and hoodies' - all six are false, and all six would have been caught by a single query against Nike's own catalogue. Under a documented condition where no product page could be opened, the only defensible conclusion was 'not found', never 'does not exist'.

Pervasive time-base drift. 2024 WNBA figures used as current in 2026; a 2019 Jordan 23 Engineered collection presented as current competitive design language; a 2014 Griner interview as a current athlete voice; 2015-2017 Asiya prototypes as a live gap; 2023 CunBA coverage as 'still spreading'; a 2019 NBA public-relations estimate as participation; a 2022 SS NOCTA product as evidence of a resale market; a June 2025 price action as a standing condition through SS28.

No non-Western primary consumer input at all. The entire Worldball thesis - the largest share of the portfolio - contains zero Chinese, Japanese, Filipino, Indian or European consumer voices, zero Chinese-language sources, zero Tmall/JD/Douyin/Xiaohongshu data and zero retrieved local prices, while carrying specific RMB, PHP, JPY and AUD price recommendations.

The cost side of the business is entirely absent from specialist work. The word 'tariff' appears nowhere in A02's output, in a year when the US de minimis exemption ended, apparel from China carries roughly a 53.5% duty stack, Nike is absorbing an estimated USD 1.5B annualised tariff cost with a 120bp gross-margin headwind, and Nike has already raised apparel prices 3%. Every price position was set without a landed-cost input.

The SS28 calendar is missing from all seven files. The FIBA World Cup runs in Qatar 27 August-12 September 2027 and the LA28 Games open 14 July 2028 in Nike's home market, inside the SS28 selling season, with Nike an Official Outfitter of the US Olympic and Paralympic Team. A04's own evidence shows the mechanism working for a competitor in an adjacent sport - adidas apparel +35% in a quarter on World Cup demand while its basketball fell 21% - and never applied it.

Duplicate-as-corroboration is the base's most dangerous structural flaw. Where three domains agree, they are usually reading the same document. The women's case, the market-size case, the China participation case, the retro-length case and the local-labels case are each one source agreed with three times, and each currently reads to a decision-maker as triangulation.
evidence_base_quality.quant_vs_qual_balance:
Roughly 30% of the base is hard, verifiable quantitative evidence - audited filings, league releases, peer-reviewed studies with named samples, and primary rulebooks - and essentially all of it describes the company, the sport, the athlete's body or the rules, not the product. Another ~20% is quantitative in appearance only: syndicated report-mill CAGRs and market sizes, Accio-generated trend indices, platform search-growth percentages on undisclosed bases, and league marketing percentages on soft base years. That fifth of the base should be treated as zero, not as weak evidence, because it carries false precision into decks. The remaining ~50% is qualitative and observational - product copy, retailer listings and facets, review snippets, trend blogs, style guides, brand interviews - and it is doing most of the work behind the product-level conclusions.

The imbalance that matters is not quant-versus-qual in aggregate; it is that the quantitative strength and the decision needs sit in different places. The base can tell you precisely what Nike earned, how many people attended an NBL game, how many lateral movements a professional guard makes and how much sweat a uniform traps. It cannot tell you a single thing, in any market, about how many basketball shorts sell, at what inseam, at what realised price, through which door, to whom, or why they come back. The one category the entire programme is about is the one category with no quantitative evidence at all. Every opportunity therefore rests on a qualitative gap claim plus an unanchored price - and where those gap claims have been checked against Nike's live catalogue, most have failed. The correction is not more research; it is four internal pulls (shorts units and ASP by inseam and region; markdown and full-price sell-through by SKU; returns coded by reason; women's and youth size-curve fill and rebuy) which between them would resolve more open questions than the seven domains resolved in total.

The 'reviews do not mention it' inference is correlation-as-causation off a tiny sample.
